newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.

text.p: Contracts on Shanghai's treasury bill repurchase market ended down on Tuesday with a break in the recent flood of new A share issues in Shenzhen, traders said.
The 28-day contract was the most active, falling to 9.4 percent from 13.71 percent.
Total turnover fell sharply to 4.34 million lots from 11.65 million lots. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
The market followed falls in the early-maturing contracts as the stream of new A share issues in Shenzhen since the beginning of the year dried up, traders said.
But they said they expected the early-maturing contracts to move up before the Chinese new year holiday in early February.
"The 14-day and 28-day contracts fell most sharply today, but major institutions that expect the A share market to rise bought the contracts ahead of the close," one trader said.
Shanghai T-bill spots closed mostly higher on Tuesday. Traders said the market would continue to rebound after sharp losses in the past few sessions.
The three-year note that matures in September 1999 was the most active, ending up at 102.78 yuan from 102.24 yuan. The turnover of the note was 44 million yuan.
The total volume of the eight-contract market rose to 971,793 lots from 675,389 lots.
Traders said the day's rises marked a rebound following sharp falls since mid-January. They said the upward trend would continue in the next few days.
